Explain exactly what you intend to do and to answer
  • State the questions you will aim to answer
  • Consider the practicalities of the proposed study
  • Select the primary outcome measure
  • Note how you will collect and use the information
  • Identify the type of support you think you will need
  • Declare any sort of influence you have, or are perceived to have, over the finding and the research


I will investigate why different people report different assessments of risk and how they think about probabilities, when the same event is predicted, but by different observers (AKA experts).

Explain what assumptions you are making about the independence, relevance, exclusivity, objectivity and importance of the evidence you plan to include in your study. For a study that creates data, explain your assumptions about patterns and relationships. In the interests of reproducibility, describe the uncertainties you have about the evidence and how you plan to minimise those.


We are all free to assess any data relevant to the research objectives and inferences that we judge reasonable considering the data and how we judge the evidence to be relevant. Importantly, we are free to use any value of statistical risk (which is the multiplication of a probability by a harm index to arrive at a measure of severity) and choose the death rate as the metric for sophistication of information about survival. Death registration provides ample evidence of data that will be relevant for values of survival as the metric for sophistication of information about survival. Our measure of sophistication should be commensurate with that data. The measure of sophistication of actual information is determined by how much data is actually obtained and what measures of the quality of data are extracted or recorded. Indeed, the bigger the register, the less risk of sample error. The metric used for sophistication is the magnitude of regression of prosperity on the measure of sophistication. This is because the bigger the registers, the more difficult it is for humans to make survival despite the magnitude being for a different measure.

Explain how you aim to achieve the objective, using cause-and-effect terms where appropriate.


We shall study the reliance on first hand direct information obtained immediately from individuals. The bigger the registration, the better the measure of risk conferred to help predict survival. We will follow the following stages.

  • To identify historical correlations between wellness and relative prosperity to examine the dependence of wellness (our statistical associations that are not mediated by any variable) on relative prosperity (the amount of life register).
